correctness.rationale: A minimal nontrivial reciprocal-divisibility solution must have 1<a<b. Setting c=(a^2-a+1)/b gives 1<=c<a, bc==1 mod a, and from a|F(b) one gets a|c^2 F(b)==F(c) mod a; also c|F(a). Thus (c,a) is a strictly smaller solution unless c=1, which forces a|F(1)=1, a contradiction. Separately S(n)=n^-1 sum_{d|n}d phi(d), multiplicative numerator on prime powers (p^{2e+1}+1)/(p+1)==1 mod p, excluding p and p^2. For pq, S(pq)=F(p)F(q)/(pq) and integrality would imply the forbidden reciprocal pair. All cases Omega<=2 exhausted. Independent finite tests to a,b<=300 and n<=500 corroborate, not replace descent.

final_claim: The only positive integer reciprocal divisibility pair a|b^2-b+1 and b|a^2-a+1 is (1,1). Consequently the gcd-reciprocal sum S(n)=sum_{i=1}^n 1/gcd(n,i) cannot be integral for n>1 with Omega(n)<=2.
